Two marks

This page carries two glyphs and nothing else worth measuring, which is on purpose: each one is a specific way a mark can render at the right size, in the right place in the DOM, and still fail the contrast a reader actually needs to see it. Neither defect shows up by reading the stylesheet. Both only show up by reading the pixels a browser actually paints.

An unlabelled mark, on its own, at the edge of visible:

This first mark measures under two to one against the white page behind it, which clears no contrast floor at any size. It is the shape of defect that put glyph measurement into this rule at all: a mark that every earlier check counted as present because it existed in the document at the right size and the right position, without ever asking whether a reader could actually see the shape it draws.

A two-tone mark whose plate has been overridden to full opacity:

This second mark is supposed to be two tones: a plate at half opacity under a solid inner shape, which is how a duotone glyph is normally drawn. Its plate has been forced back to full opacity here, so the two paths collapse into one flat shape, and the separation a duotone glyph depends on is gone even though each path still passes an ordinary contrast check on its own.
